kings2.2.p1.b1.text: Shortly before the LORD took Elijah up to heaven in a whirlwind, Elijah and Elisha were on their way from Gilgal,

kings2.2.p1.b2.text: “Please stay here, for the LORD has sent me on to Bethel.”

kings2.2.p1.b3.text: “As surely as the LORD lives and as you yourself live, I will not leave you.”

kings2.2.p1.b4.text: “Do you know that the LORD will take your master away from you today?”

kings2.2.p1.b5.text: “Yes, I know,” he replied. “Do not speak of it.”

kings2.2.p2.b2.text: “Yes, I know,” he replied. “Do not speak of it.”

kings2.2.p2.b3.text: Then a company of fifty of the sons of the prophets went and stood at a distance, facing Elijah and Elisha as the two of them stood by the Jordan.

kings2.2.p2.b4.text: And Elijah took his cloak, rolled it up, and struck the waters, which parted to the right and to the left, so that the two of them crossed over on dry ground.

kings2.2.p3.b1.text: “Tell me, what can I do for you before I am taken away from you?”

kings2.2.p3.b2.text: “Please, let me inherit a double portion of your spirit,”

kings2.2.p3.b3.text: “You have requested a difficult thing,” said Elijah. “Nevertheless, if you see me as I am taken from you, it will be yours. But if not, then it will not be so.”

kings2.2.p4.b1.text: As they were walking along and talking together, suddenly a chariot of fire with horses of fire appeared and separated the two of them, and Elijah went up into heaven in a whirlwind.

kings2.2.p4.b2.text: “My father, my father, the chariots and horsemen of Israel!”

kings2.2.p4.b3.text: And he saw Elijah no more.

kings2.2.p5.b1.text: So taking hold of his own clothes, he tore them in two.

kings2.2.p5.b2.text: Elisha also picked up the cloak that had fallen from Elijah, and he went back and stood on the bank of the Jordan.

kings2.2.p5.b3.text: “Where now is the LORD, the God of Elijah?”

kings2.2.p5.b4.text: And when he had struck the waters, they parted to the right and to the left, and Elisha crossed over.

kings2.2.p6.b1.text: “The spirit of Elijah rests on Elisha.”

kings2.2.p6.b2.text: “… Perhaps the Spirit of the LORD has taken him up and put him on one of the mountains or in one of the valleys.”

kings2.2.p6.b4.text: … who searched for three days but did not find Elijah.

kings2.2.p6.b5.text: “Didn’t I tell you not to go?”

kings2.2.p7.b1.text: “Please note, our lord, that the city’s location is good, as you can see. But the water is bad and the land is unfruitful.”

kings2.2.p7.b2.text: “Bring me a new bowl,” he replied, “and put some salt in it.” …

kings2.2.p7.b3.text: “This is what the LORD says: ‘I have healed this water. No longer will it cause death or unfruitfulness.’”

kings2.2.p7.b4.text: And the waters there have been healthy to this day, according to the word spoken by Elisha.

kings2.2.p8.b1.text: From there, Elisha went up to Bethel, …

kings2.2.p8.b2.text: “Go up, you baldhead! Go up, you baldhead!”

kings2.2.p9.b1.text: Then he turned around, looked at them, and called down a curse on them in the name of the LORD.

kings2.2.p9.b2.text: Suddenly two female bears came out of the woods and mauled forty-two of the boys.

kings2.2.p9.b3.text: And Elisha went on to Mount Carmel, and from there he returned to Samaria.
